title: Uniform boundedness criterion for internal Hom universal coefficients
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, and use ordinary derived categories of module sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. A sheaf is constructible if it has a finite locally closed stratification [def-constructible-stratification] on which it is locally constant with finitely generated $A$-module stalks [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules, def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $K$ be bounded above with constructible cohomology and let $Y$ have finite Tor amplitude, meaning that $Y\otimes^L_{A_X}F$ has cohomology in one fixed finite interval for every module sheaf $F$ in degree zero [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Suppose there are integers $d\le e$ such that $R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M_X\otimes^L_{A_X}Y)$ has cohomology in $[d,e]$ for every ordinary $A$-module $M$ in degree zero; $M_X$ is its constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Then $H=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,Y)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] has finite Tor amplitude (tested against all module sheaves). For every bounded below complex $C\in D^+(A)$ of ordinary $A$-modules the canonical map $$u_C:C_X\otimes^L_{A_X}H\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_A(K,C_X\otimes^L_{A_X}Y)$$ is an isomorphism, natural in $K,Y,C$. The map $u_C$ is the tensor--Hom transpose of evaluation tensored with $C_X$, using the signed tensor symmetry. In particular $C$ need not be perfect or have finite Tor amplitude.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 10.1.1, pp. 325-326 (uniformly bounded alternative); canonical map defined in the first paragraph of its proof. No Stacks tag states this universal-coefficients criterion in this generality.

proof.text: Put $H=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,Y)$, $F(C)=C_X\otimes^L_AH$ and $G(C)=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,C_X\otimes^L_AY)$. The hypothesis with $M=A$ gives $H\in D^{[d,e]}$. Choose $r$ with $K\in D^{\le r}$ and $[a,b]$ a Tor interval for $Y$. Constant module sheafification is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-constant-exact]; hence it sends cone triangles of ordinary complexes to cone triangles. Derived tensor is triangulated by [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated], and derived internal Hom is exact and shift-compatible by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Thus $F,G$ are exact functors. Use throughout the actual $u_C$ in the statement: transpose $K\otimes^L(C_X\otimes^LH)\to C_X\otimes^LY$ obtained from evaluation and signed symmetry. Naturality of evaluation and of transposition gives the comparison squares for every coefficient map; the same construction on cone complexes, with the tensor differential and its signed symmetry, gives a morphism of cone triangles. No arbitrary choice of an isomorphism replaces $u_C$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 10.1.1, proof p. 325, definition of the canonical morphism; exact functor conventions.

proof.text: Let $V=\bigoplus_{i\in I}A$ be any free ordinary module, including $I=\varnothing$. Its constant sheaf is $\bigoplus_I A_X$: both are sheafifications of the constant-presheaf direct sum [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Tensor commutes with these sums by [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits]. A free sheaf is flat since its tensor functor is a sum of identity functors; placed in degree zero it is a bounded-above flat complex, hence K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], so by [def-kun-derived-tensor] the degree-zero free tensor computes the derived tensor. Consequently $F(V)=\bigoplus_I H$ and $V_X\otimes^LY=\bigoplus_IY$. The family of copies of $Y$ has common lower bound $a$. Apply [lem-per-constructible-rhom-coproduct-continuity] to identify $G(V)$ with $\bigoplus_IH$. Under these identifications $u_V$ is the identity: on each basis inclusion $A\to V$, its transpose is evaluation, hence its restriction is the corresponding coproduct inclusion of $H$. The coproduct universal property determines the map. This proves invertibility for arbitrary-rank free modules, not just finite free ones.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 10.1.1, proof p. 325, first paragraph, the free-module case.

proof.text: A projective ordinary module $Q$ is a retract of a free module: take $i:Q\to V$, $s:V\to Q$, $si=1$ from [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Naturality gives an inverse to $u_Q$, namely $F(s)u_V^{-1}G(i)$; the two composites reduce respectively to $G(si)$ and $F(si)$. Hence $u_Q$ is invertible. For a bounded complex $P$ of projective ordinary modules, induct on the number of possibly nonzero terms using its finite stupid filtration. Each successive triangle adds one shifted projective module, on which the result holds by the retract calculation and shifts. The exact cohomology sequences of [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] give invertibility at the third vertex from invertibility at the other two (or apply [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] to each five-term window), and [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] detects the resulting isomorphism. The zero complex starts the induction. Thus $u_P$ is invertible for every bounded projective complex.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 10.1.1, proof p. 325, end of first paragraph; projective retract variant of the free-complex argument.

proof.text: For any $E\in D(A)^{\le q}$, [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-above-projective-model] gives a projective representative $L$ with $L^j=0$ for $j>q$. Its constant terms are flat: a projective module is a retract of a free module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], and the corresponding constant sheaf is a retract of a sum of $A_X$; tensor with the sum is exact and a retract preserves exactness. Thus $L_X$ is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Represent $H\in D^{\le e}$ by a complex zero above $e$, using [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. The total tensor $L_X\otimes H$ computes $F(E)$ by [def-kun-derived-tensor], and its degree $j$ is zero for $j>q+e$, since there are no indices $s\le q$, $t\le e$ with $s+t=j$. Therefore $F(E)\in D^{\le q+e}$. This argument makes no lower boundedness assumption on $E$ or finite-Tor assumption on $H$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 10.1.1, proof p. 325, bound on the left vertical cone, with the total-degree argument expanded.

proof.text: Now let $C\in D^b(A)$ and fix an arbitrary integer $q$. Choose a bounded-above projective model $L\simeq C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-above-projective-model]. Its brutal subcomplex $P=L^{\ge q+1}$ is bounded and projective. The map $P\to C$ has a cone $E\in D^b(A)^{\le q}$: its cone is quasi-isomorphic to $L/P$, which is zero in degrees above $q$, and it is bounded in cohomology because both $P,C$ are bounded. Step 4 gives $F(E)\le q+e$. Apply [lem-pur-bounded-heart-amplitude] to the exact functor $G$ and all ordinary modules, whose images lie in $[d,e]$ by hypothesis. Since $E$ is bounded, it gives $G(E)\le q+e$ as well. In the natural square from $P\to C$, the two vertical arrows therefore induce cohomology isomorphisms in every degree $i>q+e+1$, by the long exact sequences [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. The top comparison $u_P$ is invertible by Step 3, so $H^i(u_C)$ is invertible in that range. For a fixed $i$ choose $q<i-e-1$; this proves invertibility in every degree and hence invertibility of $u_C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. Crucially the finite Postnikov bound is applied only to the bounded cone $E$, never to an unbounded-below complex.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 10.1.1, proof p. 325, bounded-coefficient approximation square and vertical cone bounds.

proof.text: In particular, for every ordinary module $M$ placed in degree zero, Step 5 and the hypothesis give $M_X\otimes^LH\in D^{[d,e]}$. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ and any ordinary $A$-module $N$. Take $M=N$. Exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], the constant-sheaf stalk $N$ from [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk] (the abelian-group isomorphism respects the $A$-action because multiplication by every scalar commutes with coefficient germs), and [lem-sfb-etale-derived-tensor-stalk] give $N\otimes_A^LH_{\bar x}\in D^{[d,e]}$. Now let $B$ be any $A_X$-module sheaf in degree zero and take $N=B_{\bar x}$ separately at each point. The same derived tensor-stalk isomorphism yields $(B\otimes^LH)_{\bar x}=B_{\bar x}\otimes_A^LH_{\bar x}\in D^{[d,e]}$. Exact stalks and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] detect zero cohomology sheaves, so $B\otimes^LH\in D^{[d,e]}$ globally. This proves the requested Tor amplitude against all module sheaves, not only constant ones.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 10.1.1, proof p. 326, first sentence; its implicit stalkwise finite-Tor test expanded.

proof.text: We record the bounds needed to pass to $D^+(A)$. By [lem-sp-ringed-site-tor-flat-model], take bounded flat sheaf representatives of $H$ in $[d,e]$ and of $Y$ in $[a,b]$; they are K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. If $T\in D(A)^{\ge t}$, exact constant sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-constant-exact] and the standard truncations [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] give a representative $T_X$ zero below $t$. Total degrees then give $F(T)\ge t+d$ and $T_X\otimes^LY\ge t+a$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], choose for the latter object an injective representative $J$ zero below $t+a$, which is K-injective. Choose a representative of $K$ zero above $r$ by the standard truncation statement. The formula [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] computes $G(T)$ by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(K,J)$; its degree $n$ is a product of $\mathcal Hom(K^p,J^{p+n})$, all zero when $n<t+a-r$. Thus $G(T)\ge t+a-r$, uniformly in $T$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 10.1.1, proof p. 326, lower bounds on source and target before the final truncation.

proof.text: Let $C\in D^+(A)$ and let $n$ tend to $+\infty$. Its standard triangle [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] is $C_n=\tau_{\le n}C\to C\to T_n\to C_n[1]$, where $C_n$ is bounded and $T_n\ge n+1$. Step 7 gives $F(T_n)\ge n+1+d$ and $G(T_n)\ge n+1+a-r$. For a fixed degree $i$, choose $n$ so large that $i<n+1+\min(d,a-r)$. The long exact sequences [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] show that $H^iF(C_n)\to H^iF(C)$ and $H^iG(C_n)\to H^iG(C)$ are both isomorphisms. Naturality of the specified comparison gives a commuting square with these two maps and $u_{C_n},u_C$. Step 5 makes $u_{C_n}$ invertible, so $H^i(u_C)$ is invertible. Varying $i$ and using [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] proves that $u_C$ is invertible. The map has remained the evaluation transpose from Step 1 throughout. Evaluation, signed symmetry and transposition are natural in $K,Y,C$; consequently the isomorphisms just proved are natural in all three variables. No perfection or finite Tor amplitude of $C$ was used.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 10.1.1, proof p. 326, final truncation argument.

proof_origin.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 10.1.1, pp. 325-326, uniformly bounded alternative; projective retracts, stalkwise Tor detection and the final degree bounds expanded.
